simple.meaning: סַרְבַּל (çarbal) is a Hebrew word meaning “a cloak.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סַרְבַּל (H5622) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:21, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סַרְבַּל (H5622) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סַרְבַּל (H5622) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סַרְבַּל (çarbal) / H5622 is traced through Daniel 3:21, Daniel 3:27 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5622. sarbal [ סַרְבָּל ] noun [masculine] probably mantle (see especially SAC JPhil. xxvi (1899), 307 f. , compare Andr M 74* , with conjecture as to original Persian form; > trousers ; Late Hebrew; Jewish-Aramaic id. , with both meanings, also shoes ; Arabic mantle is loan-word Frä 47 ; Egyptian Arabic shoe is Greek loan-word according to Vollers ZMG li (1897), 298, compare Krauss ii. 412 ); — plural suffix סַרְבָּלֵיהוֺן Dan 3:21 , 27 .

occurrences.englishText: Then these men were bound in their pants, their tunics, and their mantles, and their other clothes, and were cast into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.

The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed, the smell of fire wasn’t even on them.
